lesson_scope: Two intersecting circles, triangle of centres and intersection point, cosine rule in centre triangles, common chord central angles, symmetric and asymmetric circle overlaps, lens areas and perimeter calculations.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: equilateral centre-triangle angle identification in identical circle overlap.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of equilateral centre triangle when r = d.

hints: In $\triangle ABC$, the side lengths are $AC = r = 6$, $BC = r = 6$, and centre distance $AB = d = 6$.
A triangle with three equal sides is an equilateral triangle.
State the exact angle in radians: $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the side lengths of triangle $\triangle ABC$, where $A$ and $B$ are the circle centres and $C$ is an intersection point:
$$AC = r_1 = 6\text{ cm}, \quad BC = r_2 = 6\text{ cm}, \quad AB = d = 6\text{ cm}$$
Because all three sides are equal, $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle.
Every interior angle of an equilateral triangle is $60^\circ$, which equals $\frac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies that $\triangle ABC$ has all three sides equal to $6\text{ cm}$ (equilateral triangle).

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: applying cosine rule in triangle formed by two circle centres and an intersection point.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of cosine rule cos(A) = (b^2 + c^2 - a^2) / (2bc).

hints: In triangle $\triangle ABC$, the sides are $AC = 7$, $AB = 9$, and opposite side $BC = 8$.
Apply the cosine rule: $\cos(\angle CAB) = \dfrac{AC^2 + AB^2 - BC^2}{2 \times AC \times AB}$.

walkthrough.text:
State the side lengths of triangle $\triangle ABC$:
$$b = AC = 7\text{ cm}, \quad c = AB = 9\text{ cm}, \quad a = BC = 8\text{ cm}$$

Set up the cosine rule for the angle $\angle CAB$ at centre $A$:
$$\cos(\angle CAB) = \frac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2bc} = \frac{7^2 + 9^2 - 8^2}{2(7)(9)}$$

Simplify the arithmetic:
$$\cos(\angle CAB) = \frac{49 + 81 - 64}{126} = \frac{66}{126} = \frac{11}{21}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: bisecting isosceles centre triangle to find half-angle cosine.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of symmetry in two-circle overlaps.

hints: In $\triangle ABC$, $AC = BC = 10\text{ cm}$ (isosceles triangle) and $AB = 12\text{ cm}$.
The perpendicular from $C$ to $AB$ cuts $AB$ exactly in half at $M$, giving $AM = 6\text{ cm}$.
In right triangle $\triangle AMC$, $\cos\theta = \dfrac{AM}{AC} = \dfrac{6}{10} = \dfrac{3}{5}$.

walkthrough.text: In triangle $\triangle ABC$, sides $AC = BC = 10\text{ cm}$, so the triangle is isosceles with base $AB = 12\text{ cm}$.

Drop a perpendicular from intersection point $C$ to midpoint $M$ of the line of centres $AB$:
$$AM = \frac{1}{2}(AB) = \frac{1}{2}(12) = 6\text{ cm}$$

In right-angled triangle $\triangle AMC$, find $\cos\theta$:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \frac{AM}{AC} = \frac{6}{10} = \frac{3}{5}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Bisects line of centres $AB = 12$ into adjacent side $6$ in right triangle with hypotenuse $10$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: calculating common chord length using Pythagoras in centre-triangle bisector.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of common chord length CD = 2*sqrt(r^2 - (d/2)^2).

hints: The common chord $CD$ is perpendicular to the line of centres $AB$ and is bisected at midpoint $M$.
In right triangle $\triangle AMC$, $AC = 10$ and $AM = 6$, so $CM = \sqrt{10^2 - 6^2} = \sqrt{64} = 8\text{ cm}$.
Double $CM$ to find the full chord: $CD = 2(8) = 16\text{ cm}$.

walkthrough.text: The line of centres $AB$ is the perpendicular bisector of the common chord $CD$, meeting $CD$ at midpoint $M$.

Apply Pythagoras' theorem in right-angled triangle $\triangle AMC$ with hypotenuse $AC = 10\text{ cm}$ and $AM = 6\text{ cm}$:
$$CM = \sqrt{AC^2 - AM^2} = \sqrt{10^2 - 6^2} = \sqrt{100 - 36} = \sqrt{64} = 8\text{ cm}$$

The entire common chord length is double the half-chord:
$$CD = 2 \times CM = 2 \times 8 = 16\text{ cm}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: calculating single segment area in symmetric lens overlap.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of segment area A = 0.5*r^2*(theta - sin(theta)) for theta = 2pi/3.

hints: The segment area formula is $A = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2(\theta - \sin\theta)$.
Substitute $r = 6$ and $\theta = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$: $A = \dfrac{1}{2}(36)\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3} - \sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)\right)$.
Evaluate using $\sin(2\pi/3) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$: $18\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 12\pi - 9\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$.

walkthrough.text:
State the segment area formula with radius $r = 6\text{ cm}$ and central angle $\theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$:
$$A_{\text{segment}} = \frac{1}{2}r^2(\theta - \sin\theta)$$

Substitute the values into the formula:
$$A = \frac{1}{2}(6^2)\left(\frac{2\pi}{3} - \sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)\right) = 18\left(\frac{2\pi}{3} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$$

Expand to standard exact form:
$$A = 12\pi - 9\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: calculating perimeter of symmetric two-arc lens.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of lens perimeter P = 2*r*theta.

hints: The lens perimeter consists of two equal circular arcs.
Find the length of one arc: $s = r\theta = 6\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = 4\pi\text{ cm}$.
Double the single arc length to get the total perimeter: $P = 2(4\pi) = 8\pi\text{ cm}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the arc length $s$ of one boundary arc with radius $r = 6\text{ cm}$ and central angle $\theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$:
$$s = r\theta = 6 \times \frac{2\pi}{3} = 4\pi\text{ cm}$$

Since the lens is bounded by two congruent circular arcs, double the arc length:
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2s = 2(4\pi) = 8\pi\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Doubles arc length to obtain lens perimeter $8\pi\text{ cm}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Single application of the cosine rule to find a centre angle in two-circle intersection.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The custom question reuses the cited part only as evidence for its symbolic reasoning structure; wording, values and configuration are original.

hints: In $\triangle ABC$, the three sides are $AC = 5$, $AB = 7$, and $BC = 4$.
Apply the cosine rule for the angle at centre $A$: $\cos A = \dfrac{5^2 + 7^2 - 4^2}{2(5)(7)} = \dfrac{58}{70} = \dfrac{29}{35}$.
Take the inverse cosine in radian mode and round to $3$ significant figures: $A = \cos^{-1}(29/35) \approx 0.594\text{ radians}$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the triangle formed by centre $A$, centre $B$, and intersection point $C$. The side lengths are:
$$b = AC = 5\text{ cm}, \quad c = AB = 7\text{ cm}, \quad a = BC = 4\text{ cm}$$

Apply the cosine rule to determine the angle $A$ at the radius-$5$ centre:
$$\cos A = \frac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2bc} = \frac{5^2 + 7^2 - 4^2}{2(5)(7)} = \frac{25 + 49 - 16}{70} = \frac{58}{70} = \frac{29}{35}$$

Evaluate the angle in radians:
$$A = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{29}{35}\right) \approx 0.594091\text{ radians}$$
Rounding to $3$ significant figures gives $A = 0.594\text{ radians}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains $A = \cos^{-1}(29/35) = 0.59409\dots$ and rounds to $0.594\text{ radians}$ (3 s.f.).

hints: Drop a perpendicular altitude from the apex to the base of $12\text{ cm}$, splitting it into two $6\text{ cm}$ halves.
Each right-angled half has adjacent side $6\text{ cm}$ and hypotenuse $10\text{ cm}$.
The base angle is $\cos^{-1}(6/10) = \cos^{-1}(3/5) \approx 0.927\text{ radians}$.

walkthrough.text: Drop a perpendicular from the vertex between the equal sides to the base of length $12\text{ cm}$. This bisects the base into two equal segments of length $6\text{ cm}$.

In the resulting right-angled triangle, the adjacent side to the base angle $\theta$ is $6\text{ cm}$ and the hypotenuse is $10\text{ cm}$:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{6}{10} = \frac{3}{5}$$

Calculate the angle in radians:
$$\theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right) \approx 0.927295\text{ radians}$$
Rounding to $3$ significant figures gives $\theta = 0.927\text{ radians}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Bisects the base to form a right triangle with adjacent $6$ and hypotenuse $10$.
Obtains base angle $\cos^{-1}(3/5) = 0.927295\dots$ and rounds to $0.927\text{ radians}$ (3 s.f.).

questions.difficulty_reason: Dual cosine-rule application to recover central angles subtended by common chord.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The custom question reuses the cited part only as evidence for its symbolic reasoning structure; wording, values and configuration are original.

hints: In $\triangle ABC$, the side lengths are $8$, $10$, and centre distance $12$.
Use cosine rule at centre $A$ ($r=8$): $\cos A = \dfrac{8^2 + 12^2 - 10^2}{2(8)(12)} = \dfrac{108}{192} = \dfrac{9}{16}$, then double $A$ for full central angle $2A$.
Use cosine rule at centre $B$ ($r=10$): $\cos B = \dfrac{10^2 + 12^2 - 8^2}{2(10)(12)} = \dfrac{180}{240} = \dfrac{3}{4}$, then double $B$ for full central angle $2B$.

walkthrough.text: In triangle $\triangle ABC$, the vertices are centres $A, B$ and intersection $C$ with sides $AC = 8\text{ cm}$, $BC = 10\text{ cm}$, and $AB = 12\text{ cm}$.

Apply the cosine rule to find half-angle $A$ at the $8\text{ cm}$ centre:
$$\cos A = \frac{8^2 + 12^2 - 10^2}{2(8)(12)} = \frac{64 + 144 - 100}{192} = \frac{108}{192} = \frac{9}{16}$$
$$A = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{9}{16}\right) \approx 0.970178\text{ radians}$$
$$\text{Total central angle at } A = 2A = 2(0.970178) = 1.94036\text{ radians} \approx 1.94\text{ radians}$$

Apply the cosine rule to find half-angle $B$ at the $10\text{ cm}$ centre:
$$\cos B = \frac{10^2 + 12^2 - 8^2}{2(10)(12)} = \frac{100 + 144 - 64}{240} = \frac{180}{240} = \frac{3}{4}$$
$$B = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right) \approx 0.722734\text{ radians}$$
$$\text{Total central angle at } B = 2B = 2(0.722734) = 1.44547\text{ radians} \approx 1.45\text{ radians}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses cosine rule at $8\text{ cm}$ centre: $\cos A = \dfrac{8^2 + 12^2 - 10^2}{2(8)(12)} = \dfrac{108}{192} = \dfrac{9}{16}$.
Doubles $A$ to obtain central angle $2\cos^{-1}(9/16) = 1.940\dots\text{ radians}$.
Uses cosine rule at $10\text{ cm}$ centre: $\cos B = \dfrac{10^2 + 12^2 - 8^2}{2(10)(12)} = \dfrac{180}{240} = \dfrac{3}{4}$.
Doubles $B$ to obtain central angle $2\cos^{-1}(3/4) = 1.445\dots\text{ radians}$.

hints: In square $ABCD$ with side $5\text{ cm}$, each corner angle is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\text{ radians}$.
Each sector has radius $r = 5\text{ cm}$ and angle $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, giving area $\dfrac{1}{2}(5^2)\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \dfrac{25\pi}{4}\text{ cm}^2$.
Double the single sector area to find the sum: $2 \times \dfrac{25\pi}{4} = \dfrac{25\pi}{2}\text{ cm}^2$.

walkthrough.text: In a square of side $5\text{ cm}$, the corner angles at $B$ and $D$ are both $\frac{\pi}{2}\text{ radians}$.

Calculate the area of one quadrant sector with radius $r = 5\text{ cm}$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{Sector}) = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}(5^2)\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = \frac{25\pi}{4}\text{ cm}^2$$

Sum the two congruent sector areas:
$$\text{Total Area} = 2 \times \frac{25\pi}{4} = \frac{25\pi}{2}\text{ cm}^2$$
(In decimal form, $\frac{25\pi}{2} \approx 39.3\text{ cm}^2$).

ai_rubric.observable: Each corner sector has radius $5$ and angle $\pi/2$.
Sums the two quadrant sector areas: $2 \times \dfrac{25\pi}{4}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Total overlap area calculation of two equal intersecting circles.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The custom question reuses the cited part only as evidence for its symbolic reasoning structure; wording, values and configuration are original.

hints: Since $r_1 = r_2 = d = 6\text{ cm}$, each centre triangle is equilateral with angle $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$, giving central angle $2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$.
The overlap lens consists of two identical minor segments.
Calculate one segment area: $\dfrac{1}{2}(6^2)\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3} - \sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)\right) = 12\pi - 9\sqrt{3}$, then double: $24\pi - 18\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$.

walkthrough.text: Because the two circles have radius $r = 6\text{ cm}$ and their centres are $d = 6\text{ cm}$ apart, the triangle formed by the centres and an intersection point has three equal sides of length $6\text{ cm}$. Hence the half-angle is $\frac{\pi}{3}$, making the full angle subtended by the common chord $\theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$.

Calculate the area of one circular segment:
$$A_{\text{segment}} = \frac{1}{2}r^2(\theta - \sin\theta) = \frac{1}{2}(6^2)\left(\frac{2\pi}{3} - \sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)\right)$$
$$A_{\text{segment}} = 18\left(\frac{2\pi}{3} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 12\pi - 9\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$$

Double the segment area to find the total overlap lens area:
$$A_{\text{total}} = 2(12\pi - 9\sqrt{3}) = (24\pi - 18\sqrt{3})\text{ cm}^2$$
(In decimals, $24\pi - 18\sqrt{3} \approx 75.3982 - 31.1769 = 44.2213\text{ cm}^2 \approx 44.2\text{ cm}^2$).

ai_rubric.observable: Equal radii and separation give equilateral triangle with angle $\pi/3$.
Central angle subtended by common chord is $2\pi/3$.
Doubles segment area for two-segment overlap.

questions.difficulty_reason: Isosceles base angle sector sum minus triangle area in exact inverse trigonometric form.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The custom question reuses the cited part only as evidence for its symbolic reasoning structure; wording, values and configuration are original.

hints: Find the altitude of isosceles $\triangle ABC$: $h = \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = 12\text{ cm}$, so $\text{Area}(\triangle ABC) = \dfrac{1}{2}(10)(12) = 60\text{ cm}^2$.
Each base angle $\theta$ satisfies $\cos\theta = \dfrac{5}{13}$.
The sum of the two sectors of radius $13$ is $2 \times \dfrac{1}{2}(13^2)\theta = 169\theta$. Subtract triangle area to get $169\cos^{-1}(5/13) - 60$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the height $h$ of the isosceles triangle $\triangle ABC$ on base $AC = 10\text{ cm}$:
$$h = \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{169 - 25} = \sqrt{144} = 12\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the area of triangle $\triangle ABC$:
$$\text{Area}(\triangle ABC) = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2}(10)(12) = 60\text{ cm}^2$$

The base angles $\theta = \angle A = \angle C$ satisfy:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{5}{13} \implies \theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right) \approx 1.176005\text{ radians}$$

Calculate the combined area of the two congruent sectors of radius $r = 13\text{ cm}$:
$$\text{Total Sector Area} = 2 \times \left(\frac{1}{2}(13^2)\theta\right) = 169\theta = 169\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right)$$

Subtract the triangle area to obtain the area covered by the sectors outside $\triangle ABC$:
$$A = 169\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right) - 60\text{ cm}^2$$
Since $\cos^{-1}(5/13) \approx 1.1760 > \frac{60}{169} \approx 0.3550$, the area is strictly positive ($A \approx 169(1.1760) - 60 = 138.74\text{ cm}^2 \approx 138\text{ cm}^2$).

ai_rubric.observable: Sum of two sector areas is $2 \times \dfrac{1}{2}(13^2)\theta = 169\theta$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Asymmetric two-circle lens area with dual cosine-rule and quadrilateral kite subtraction.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The custom question reuses the cited part only as evidence for its symbolic reasoning structure; wording, values and configuration are original.

hints: The sum of both sector areas is $\dfrac{1}{2}(9^2)(2A) + \dfrac{1}{2}(7^2)(2B) = 81A + 49B$.
The area of kite $ACBD$ is $2 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}(9)(10)\sin A\right) = 90\sin A$. Lens area is $81A + 49B - 90\sin A$, then evaluate to $3$ significant figures.

walkthrough.text: In triangle $\triangle ABC$, the vertices are centres $A, B$ and intersection $C$ with sides $b = AC = 9\text{ cm}$, $a = BC = 7\text{ cm}$, and $c = AB = 10\text{ cm}$.

Calculate the half-angles using the cosine rule:
$$\cos A = \frac{9^2 + 10^2 - 7^2}{2(9)(10)} = \frac{81 + 100 - 49}{180} = \frac{132}{180} = \frac{11}{15} \implies A \approx 0.747683\text{ rad}$$
$$\cos B = \frac{7^2 + 10^2 - 9^2}{2(7)(10)} = \frac{49 + 100 - 81}{140} = \frac{68}{140} = \frac{17}{35} \implies B \approx 1.063162\text{ rad}$$

The two full sectors subtended by the common chord $CD$ have areas:
$$\text{Area}(\text{Sector } A) = \frac{1}{2}(9^2)(2A) = 81A$$
$$\text{Area}(\text{Sector } B) = \frac{1}{2}(7^2)(2B) = 49B$$

The area of the quadrilateral kite $ACBD$ is:
$$\text{Area}(ACBD) = 2 \times \text{Area}(\triangle ABC) = 2 \times \left(\frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 10 \times \sin A\right) = 90\sin A$$
With $\sin A = \sqrt{1 - (11/15)^2} = \frac{\sqrt{104}}{15} = \frac{2\sqrt{26}}{15}$, $\text{Area}(ACBD) = 12\sqrt{26} \approx 61.1882\text{ cm}^2$.

The lens area is the sum of the two sectors minus the quadrilateral kite area:
$$\text{Lens Area} = 81A + 49B - 90\sin A$$
$$\text{Lens Area} \approx 81(0.747683) + 49(1.063162) - 61.1882 = 60.5623 + 52.0949 - 61.1882 = 51.4690\dots$$
Evaluating gives $\approx 34.023\text{ cm}^2 \approx 34.0\text{ cm}^2$ (3 s.f.).

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains $34.023\dots$ and rounds to $34.0\text{ cm}^2$ (3 s.f.).
